arabic_blocks: [993] حدثنا عمرو بن عون قال: حدثنا خالد عن يونس عن الحسن عن أبي بكرة قال كنا عند رسول الله ﷺ فانكسفت الشمس فقام النبي ﷺ يجر رداءه حتى دخل المسجد فدخلنا فصلى بنا ركعتين حتى انجلت الشمس، فقال ﷺ إن الشمس والقمر لا ينكسفان لموت أحد فإذا رأيتموهما فصلوا وادعوا حتى يكشف ما بكم
english_blocks: ‘Amr ibn ‘Awn related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, who said:

We were with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the sun was eclipsed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up, dragging his cloak, until he entered the mosque. We entered, and he led us in two rak‘ahs until the sun became clear. Then he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death. When you see them, pray and supplicate until what has befallen you is removed.”

Then he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see that, remember Allah.”

They said: “Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something where you stood, then we saw you draw back.” He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw Paradise and reached for a cluster. Had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remains. I was shown the Fire, and I have never seen a sight more dreadful than today’s. I saw that most of its inhabitants were women.”

They said: “Why, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Because of their ingratitude.” It was said: “Do they disbelieve in Allah?” He said: “They are ungrateful to their husbands and ungrateful for kindness. If you were kind to one of them for all time, then she saw something from you, she would say: ‘I have never seen any good from you.’”

english_blocks: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us. He said: Ziyad ibn ‘Ilaqah related to us. He said: I heard al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah saying:

The people said: “It was eclipsed because of Ibrahim’s death.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see them, supplicate to Allah and pray until it clears.”

english_blocks: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Yunus related to us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, who said:

The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He went out dragging his cloak until he reached the mosque. The people gathered around him, and he led them in two rak‘ahs. Then the sun cleared.
He said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death. When that happens, pray and supplicate until what has come upon you is removed.”
That was because a son of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had died, called Ibrahim, and the people spoke about that.

english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Mihran related to us. He said: al-Walid related to us. He said: Ibn Namir informed us; he heard Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited aloud in the eclipse prayer. When he finished his recitation, he proclaimed Allah’s greatness and bowed. When he rose from the bowing, he said: “Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.” Then he resumed recitation. In the eclipse prayer there were four bowings in two rak‘ahs and four prostrations.
Al-Awza‘i and others said: I heard al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, that:

The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He sent a caller to announce: “Prayer in congregation.” Then he went forward and prayed four bowings in two rak‘ahs and four prostrations.
And ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Namir informed me that he heard the same from Ibn Shihab.

Al-Zuhri said: I said: “Your brother, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, did not do that. He prayed only two rak‘ahs, like the dawn prayer, when he prayed in Madinah.” He said: “Yes, he was mistaken about the Sunnah.”
Sufyan ibn Husayn and Sulayman ibn Kathir followed him in transmitting from al-Zuhri about reciting aloud.
